questions.prompt: 다음을 듣고, 여자가 하는 말의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 보건실 이용에 대해 안내하려고
구급약 사용 방법을 설명하려고
보건실 환경 개선을 건의하려고
학생 식당 위치를 알려주려고
학사 일정 변경을 공지하려고
questions.script:
W: Good morning, students! This is your school nurse, Emma Lee.
What do you think of high school life so far? Since this is your first
semester, I’m going to give you some guidelines for visiting our
school clinic. First, the clinic is located on the third floor next to
the school cafeteria. And it’s open Monday through Friday, from 9
a.m. to 4 p.m. I’ll be there to help you with anything you need like
medicine or some treatment. Lastly, when you are in the clinic,
please be careful not to disturb the other students. I hope you have
a safe and healthy school life. Thank you.

questions.prompt: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 물건을 충동적으로 구매하지 않아야 한다.
지출을 기록하는 것은 금전 관리에 도움이 된다.
부모로부터 경제적으로 독립하는 것이 필요하다.
현명한 소비는 자기 만족감을 향상시킬 수 있다.
기억력 향상을 위해 메모하는 습관을 길러야 한다.
questions.script:
M: Hey, sweetie. Why are you so quiet?
W: Dad, I feel bad today.
M: What’s the matter?
W: I can’t buy the running shoes I want.
M: How come? You just got paid from your part‐time job!
W: Yeah, but I spent it all. I feel like I never have enough money.
M: Have you tried writing down where you spend your money?
W: No, I haven’t. Do you think writing it down is helpful?
M: Totally. Once you see where your money goes, you’ll be more
careful with it.
W: Oh, that’s a good point, Dad.
M: It’s crucial to keep a record of your spending. That’ll help you
manage your money wisely.
W: Okay, I’ll remember that.

questions.prompt: 다음을 듣고, 여자가 하는 말의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 질문은 의사소통을 원활하게 만들어 준다.
어려운 과업일수록 더 꾸준한 연습이 필요하다.
지나친 조언은 오히려 대화를 단절시킬 수 있다.
성공하기 위해서 원만한 인간관계가 필수적이다.
좋은 관계 형성을 위해 경청하는 태도가 중요하다.
questions.script:
W: Good evening, everyone! This is Christina Turner, and you’re tuning
in to Christina’s Radio Show. Tonight, one of our listeners asked
how to keep relationships strong and healthy. Actually, many people
want to know the answer. The most important way to build good
relationships is to show that you’re listening. As you know,
communication works two ways. It’s not just about speaking, but
also about paying attention to what others are saying. You have to
try to understand and show that you really care. It can be
challenging at first. But the more carefully you listen, the better
your relationships will be. Now, let’s hear a few stories and tips
from our listeners.

questions.prompt: 대화를 듣고, 그림에서 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
questions.script:
M: Hello, Jane. How was your weekend?
W: Hi, Walter. It was nice. My family watched a movie together
outdoors. Here’s the photo.
M: Wow! That looks fantastic. Did you set up the screen in the center
by yourself?
W: No, my kids helped me out. It took some time, but we got it done.
M: The lights above the screen are perfect. They really set the mood.
W: You’re right about that.
M: I’m sure your kids liked the lights.
W: They did. I also put some popcorn on the table for their snacks.
M: That’s very sweet. Oh, you used the heart‐shaped picnic mat I gave
you!
W: It was so useful. Thanks.
M: Is that your dog sitting next to the picnic mat?
W: Yeah, he loved being outdoors, too. We had so much fun together.

questions.prompt: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 할 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 상품 준비하기
무대 장식하기
참가 신청서 받기
심사 위원 선정하기
스피커 점검하기
questions.script:
M: Katie, are we almost done with the preparations for our school’s
dance competition?
W: I guess so, Justin. But I’m still worried things might not go well.
M: Let’s do a final check together, then. Do you have the list of
performing teams?
W: Yes, I have it right here.
M: I see. And who’s going to judge the performance?
W: Well, I’ve asked some teachers for their help. And I’ve prepared
prizes for the top three teams.
M: Good! And I put up the stage decorations with my friends.
W: I already had a look. And they’re great!
M: How about the audio? Are the speakers working properly?
W: Oh no! I’ve been so busy that I completely forgot to check the
speakers.
M: No worries. Let me take care of it.
W: Thank you.

questions.prompt: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
questions.script:
M: Hello! Welcome to Tom’s Party Supplies. How can I help you?
W: Hi. I want to get something for my grandma’s birthday party.
M: You’ve come to the right place. What do you have in mind?
W: I’m looking for some balloons and gift bags.
M: I see. This set of birthday balloons is very popular, and it’s only
$20 per set.
W: Excellent. I’ll take two sets. Can you show me some gift bags?
M: Certainly. These are our gift bags. We can also make special ones
for you, if you’d like.
W: Awesome. Is it possible to put my grandma’s picture on this bag?
M: Sure. That would be $2 for each bag with a picture.
W: Great. Then, I’ll take 30.
M: So two sets of balloons and 30 special gift bags, right?
W: Yes. I have this discount coupon. Can I use it now?
M: Of course. That’ll give you 10% off the total.
W: Good. Here’s my credit card.

questions.prompt: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 시상식에 갈 수 없는 이유를 고르시오.
choices: 대학 입학 면접이 있어서
아르바이트를 해야 해서
여동생 병문안을 가야 해서
도서관 자원봉사를 해야 해서
공연 리허설과 일정이 겹쳐서
questions.script:
W: Hi, Patrick! Can we talk for a second?
M: Sure, what about?
W: I just got a call from our community center. They said that we won
first place in the creative writing contest!
M: What? That’s amazing! I can’t believe it!
W: So they asked us to go to the award ceremony. It’ll be at the
community center next Friday at 5 p.m.
M: Oh, I’m afraid I can’t go.
W: Really? Are you doing your part‐time job that day?
M: No, I only work on weekends.
W: Then, is it because you have to volunteer at the library?
M: No, it’s not that either.
W: I see. I remember you said you had to go see your sister at the
hospital.
M: No, I went to see her last week. It’s actually because I have a
university entrance interview that day.
W: Oh, I totally understand. I’ll attend the ceremony for both of us.

questions.prompt: 대화를 듣고, Darlington Park Festival에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
choices: 운영 프로그램
날짜
입장료
주차 요금
신청 방법
questions.script:
M: Hey, Sandie! I saw a poster for Darlington Park Festival. Have you
heard about it?
W: No, I haven’t, Jonathan. Why don’t you tell me about it?
M: Well, there will be programs like face painting, kite flying, and band
performances.
W: Sounds amazing! When is it?
M: This Saturday, June 28th. Do you want to go?
W: I’d love to! Do you know if there’s an admission fee?
M: It’s free for everyone. We just need to sign up for it.
W: Great. I wonder how we do that.
M: We can just scan the QR code on the poster and register our names.
W: Awesome. Then, where should we meet? I’ve never been there.
M: Don’t worry. I can give you a ride from your place.
W: That’s so sweet of you! See you then.

questions.prompt: Bake a Cake Competition에 관한 다음 내용을 듣고, 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
choices: 8월 31일에 개최된다.
기본 재료는 제공된다.
조리법을 대회 당일 제출해야 한다.
세 명의 심사 위원이 케이크를 시식할 것이다.
웹사이트에서 참가 신청을 할 수 있다.
questions.script:
M: Hello, cake lovers! Today I’m excited to announce our Bake a Cake
Competition. This once‐a‐year event takes place on August 31st and
is open to everyone in our city. You’ll bake a cake and decorate it
to show off your baking skills and creativity. We’ll provide the basic
ingredients like flour and butter. And you’re allowed to bring
anything you might need. For judging, you should submit your recipe
to our official email two weeks before the competition day. To
evaluate your cake, three judges will have a taste of it. Then, they’ll
decide the winner based on both the recipe and the final work. You
can sign up for this event on our official website. Don’t miss out on
this great opportunity!

questions.prompt: 다음 표를 보면서 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 주문할 여행용 가방을 고르시오.
questions.script:
W: Honey, what are you doing?
M: I’m looking at a website to buy a travel bag for our summer trip to
Vietnam.
W: Let me see. What size do you think we need?
M: I don’t think we should buy a 28‐inch bag.
W: Right! An oversized bag will be uncomfortable to handle.
M: Exactly. And I don’t want to spend more than $140 on a travel bag.
W: I agree. We’ll need a lot of money when traveling. What about the
choice of materials?
M: Oh, there are only two kinds available! Which one do you prefer?
W: I think the plastic one will be better. Fabrics can get dirty easily.
M: You’re right. Also, I think we need a lock.
W: Yes, it’s a good idea to have a lock for security.
M: Then let’s order this one.

questions.prompt: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Ben이 Amy에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: How about putting our ideas together for the project?
Let me tell you how to reduce food waste at school.
Why don’t we do a campaign about recycling?
You need to get the teacher’s permission right away.
I think we should share his ideas with our classmates.
questions.script:
M: Ben and Amy are in the same environmental club in high school.
They are doing an environmental campaign project and discussing
ideas together. Ben sees that students sometimes throw away trash
without recycling. So he wants to encourage them to recycle all the
time. Meanwhile, Amy feels that asking students to reduce food
waste is also a good idea because she notices a lot of leftovers in
the school cafeteria. Ben thinks that both ideas will certainly help
students to think more about the environment. So he wants to
suggest that they include both ideas in their project. In this
situation, what would Ben most likely say to Amy?
[16~17] 다음을 듣고, 물음에 답하시오.
W: Hello, students! In our last lesson, we learned how animals use their
senses to find food. Today, we’ll talk about ways some animals
defend themselves from enemies. First, one of the most well­known
of these animals is the skunk. Skunks spray a bad­smelling liquid to
keep enemies away. Skunk spray does not cause any lasting
damage, though its smell is hard to remove. Second, chameleons
change the color of their skin to match their surroundings, making
them hard to spot. That’s one clever way to hide from their
enemies! Next, we have frogs. By making themselves look bigger,
they appear more threatening. Another animal that uses its body for
survival is the lizard. Interestingly, lizards can cut off their own tails
to escape. But don’t worry — the tail eventually grows back! So far,
we’ve looked at animals’ defense strategies. In our next lesson,
we’ll cover plants that have similar ways to protect themselves.
